status_summary: A final rule published 2026-05-26 and effective 2026-07-27 relaxes parts of the 2023 Technology Transitions restrictions: it sets interim global warming potential limits for supermarket systems, remote condensing units and cold storage warehouses that run until 2032, delays some compliance dates, and removes the installation deadline for residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pump equipment whose components were made or imported before 2025. EPA estimated engineering cost savings with a present value of about 976 million dollars at a 3 percent discount rate (2026 to 2050). A proposal of the same date would exempt road and intermodal transport refrigeration units from the leak repair requirements. Petitions for review of the final rule were filed in the D.C. Circuit by industry groups on 2026-06-25 and by an environmental group on 2026-07-20. The statutory HFC phasedown remains in place, and on 2026-07-28 EPA released allocation data ahead of a planned rulemaking that will seek comment on allowances starting in 2029.

timeline.event: EPA finalized a rule setting a review framework for application-specific allowances and revising related Technology Transitions provisions.
EPA published a final rule reconsidering Technology Transitions restrictions, effective 2026-07-27, and a proposal to exempt transport refrigeration units from leak repair rules.
Two refrigeration industry associations petitioned the D.C. Circuit (No. 26-1174) for review of parts of the 2026 Technology Transitions rule.
An environmental group petitioned the D.C. Circuit (No. 26-1188) for review of the 2026 Technology Transitions rule.
EPA published a notice of data availability on HFC allocation program data ahead of a planned rulemaking on allowances starting in 2029.
